items.question: What was the late-delivery rate for each month from January to August 2018?
items.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
         (order_delivered_customer_date::date > order_estimated_delivery_date::date) AS late
  FROM raw.orders
  WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
    AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
    AND order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
    AND order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-09-01'
)
SELECT month,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE late) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_rate
FROM delivered
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
assumptions: Late means delivery date later than estimated delivery date, compared as dates.
Delivered order means order_status = 'delivered' and a customer delivery timestamp exists.
Late rate is late orders divided by delivered orders.
Months are the order purchase months from January to August 2018.

items.question: What is the average review score of late deliveries compared with on-time deliveries?

  SELECT o.order_id,
         (o.order_delivered_customer_date::date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date::date) AS late
  FROM raw.orders o
  WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL

  SELECT DISTINCT ON (order_id) order_id, review_score

GROUP BY d.late
ORDER BY d.late

items.question: What were the top 10 product categories by revenue in 2018?
items.sql:
WITH sales_2018 AS (
  SELECT oi.product_id, oi.price
  FROM raw.orders o
  JOIN raw.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2019-01-01'
)
SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name, 'unknown') AS category,
       ROUND(SUM(s.price), 2) AS revenue
FROM sales_2018 s
JOIN raw.products p ON p.product_id = s.product_id
LEFT JOIN raw.product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
assumptions: Revenue = sum of item price excluding freight, over sales (orders not canceled or unavailable).
2018 means the calendar year 2018 (Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2018).
Category is the English category name; products without a category are labeled 'unknown'; categories without an English translation keep their Portuguese name.

items.sql: SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name, 'unknown') AS category, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM raw.order_items oi JOIN raw.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN raw.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN raw.product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: 'Best-selling' interpreted as the category with the highest revenue (sum of item prices, excluding freight) over all sales (orders not canceled or unavailable).
Category is the English category name; products without a category are 'unknown'; categories without an English translation keep their Portuguese name.
No time period was specified, so all data is used (the analysis window restriction applies only to trends and per-month figures).

items.question: How fast is our delivery?
items.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days FROM raw.orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date >= order_purchase_timestamp
assumptions: 'How fast is our delivery' interpreted as the average delivery time in days (customer delivery timestamp minus purchase timestamp) across all delivered orders.
Delivered order defined as order_status = 'delivered' with a customer delivery timestamp.
Impossible durations (delivery before purchase) are excluded as recording errors per the glossary.
No time period specified, so all data is used (totals/overall figures do not apply the analysis window).

items.question: Which state is our biggest market?
items.sql: SELECT c.customer_state AS state, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM raw.orders o JOIN raw.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN raw.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: 'Biggest market' interpreted as the state with the highest revenue (sum of item prices, excluding freight) over all data.
Sales exclude orders with status canceled or unavailable, per the glossary definition of Sale/Revenue.
Revenue is attributed to the customer's state from raw.customers.

items.question: How are review scores trending?
items.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DATE '2017-01-01' AS month_start
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-02-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-03-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-04-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-05-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-06-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-07-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-08-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-09-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-10-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-11-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2017-12-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-01-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-02-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-03-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-04-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-05-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-06-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-07-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2018-08-01'
)
SELECT m.month_start AS month,
       ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM months m
JOIN raw.orders o
  ON o.order_purchase_timestamp >= m.month_start
 AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < m.month_start + INTERVAL '1 month'
JOIN raw.order_reviews r
  ON r.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
assumptions: Review scores are attributed to the order's purchase month (order month).
The trend is shown as the average review score per month over the analysis window (Jan 2017 - Aug 2018).
All review rows for an order are included; the glossary's 'latest answered review' rule is not applied since the question asks about review scores generally.
Months with no reviews are omitted rather than shown as zero.
